obligation: Processor notice of suspected card data compromise (contractual)
citation: Merchant agreement with the payment processor (fictional term); PCI DSS v4.0.1 Requirement 12.10.1 (N81-R03)
trigger: Suspected or confirmed compromise of card data: card numbers exposed from ticket notes or paper, or a tampered terminal
deadline: Within 24 hours of suspecting a compromise (merchant agreement term). Clock starts at suspicion, not confirmation
notify: Payment processor merchant risk or support line
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not law. Applies in this scenario because 4 card numbers were in ticket notes until the purge

obligation: Card brand compromise reporting: Visa worked example (contractual)
citation: Visa What To Do If Compromised v10.0 (effective 2026-06-25), Sections A.1-A.3 and A.5; Visa Core Rules 10.3.1.2. Card brand rules applied through the processor, not law. Other brands' rules not verified
trigger: Evidence sufficient to raise a reasonable suspicion of, or to confirm, unauthorized access to Visa account data or a system that stores, processes or transmits it
deadline: Tell the processor immediately (A.3.1). Make sure the event is reported to Visa within 3 calendar days of the suspicion or confirmation (A.1.1), then send the incident report within 3 calendar days of that notice (A.2.1). If Visa requires a PCI Forensic Investigator, retain one within 5 business days (A.5.1.1)
notify: Processor; Visa Global Risk Investigations, through the processor. Other brands as the processor directs
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if a case is opened; other brands' rules were not verified

trigger: Unauthorized access of data in electronic form containing personal information of Florida residents. Personal information includes an email address or user name with a password that would permit access to an online account, and a name with a card number plus any required code (501.171(1)(g)). Good-faith access by an agent for a business purpose is not a breach (501.171(1)(a))
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and without unreasonable delay, no later than 30 days after the determination of a breach or reason to believe a breach occurred. Notice by mail or email ((4)(d)) with the content in (4)(e)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - an export of ticket notes with account passwords or card numbers is expected to qualify; counsel decides for passcode-only records

trigger: A law enforcement agency determines in writing that notice would interfere with a criminal investigation
deadline: Delay for the period the agency specifies in writing
notify: Hold individual notices; keep the written request

trigger: After investigation and consultation with law enforcement, the business reasonably determines the breach has not and will not likely result in identity theft or other financial harm
deadline: Document in writing, keep for at least 5 years, and provide to the Department of Legal Affairs within 30 days after the determination
applies_at_this_tier: Possible for records that held only names and device models; counsel decides

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable, no later than 30 days after the determination of a breach or reason to believe a breach occurred. (The 15 additional days for good cause apply only to the notice to individuals, never to this notice.) Content listed in (3)(b)
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (Attorney General)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500 or more Florida residents (likely: SYS-01 holds about 5,600 records, about 88% in Florida)

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
notify: All nationwide consumer reporting agencies (15 U.S.C. 1681a(p))

obligation: Third-party agent breach notice to the business (inbound)
trigger: A third-party agent (for example the ticketing vendor or website builder) has a breach of a system it maintains for the business
deadline: No later than 10 days following the determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred; the agent must give the business the information it needs to notify
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - track each vendor's term in the vendor list (POL-01 6.2)

citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48) (N81-R02)
trigger: Breach of computerized personal information of residents of other states (definitions vary by state)
deadline: Varies by state (for example without unreasonable delay or a fixed number of days)
notify: Affected residents; state attorney general or regulator where the state requires it; consumer reporting agencies above state-set counts
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - about 12% of customers have out-of-state addresses; counsel applies each state's law

trigger: Account takeover with theft of customer data, or fraud texts sent to customers
deadline: As soon as practical (target day 0 to 1)
notify: FBI (IC3 online report); local police if a customer loses money
applies_at_this_tier: Recommended; supports the Florida (4)(c) consultation and OFAC mitigation
Only if coverage exists - no standalone cyber policy; the owner is confirming whether the general liability policy has a cyber endorsement

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any extortion payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering any ransom or extortion payment (for example a demand not to publish the exported customer list)
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if sanctioned party); law enforcement (FBI) or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Only if an extortion demand is made. All U.S. persons. Strict liability for payments to sanctioned parties

trigger: Notification event at a financial institution involving 500 or more consumers
deadline: As soon as possible, no later than 30 days after discovery
applies_at_this_tier: No - the business offers no credit or financing and is not a financial institution (P03 G-143)

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident (reasonable belief) or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours after ransom payment
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25 (proposed only); the business is far below its SBA size standard

obligation: Covered telecommunications equipment or services discovered
citation: FAR 52.204-25(d) (Section 889); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Contractor identifies covered telecommunications equipment or services in use or delivered
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification; further report within 10 business days. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: No - the business holds no federal contracts or subcontracts

citation: FAR 52.204-23(c); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Contractor identifies a covered article from Kaspersky Lab in use or delivered
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification; further report within 10 business days. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: No - the business holds no federal contracts or subcontracts
